quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing anytime you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What can help reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Use the correct position in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct position in your lane.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance, look 12 seconds ahead, avoid hazards, and be ready for sudden changes.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you earliest.
In the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
On the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where other drivers can see you earliest.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When should you do a head check?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for blind spots before changing lanes, merging, or passing.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a helmet?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
One that hides you from other drivers.
One that places you next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Idaho, motorcycles must have fenders on both wheels, a brake on at least one wheel, a headlight, a horn, a mirror, a muffler, a brake light, a taillight, and at least one rear reflector. If you carry passengers, you also need a passenger seat and footrests.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: It is difficult to ride right after it starts raining because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers drive too slowly in wet weather.

questions.explanation: The pavement is especially slippery when rain just starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, mixing with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane behind a car, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. To be most visible, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced by:
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, you should ride on which side of your lane?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space possible. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.
Keep better control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will change to red soon.
The light will change to green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will change to red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is changing to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going through it.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space between your bike and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between your bike and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always leave yourself plenty of space around your bike to avoid collisions. Keep this space when following another vehicle, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can hurt your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can hurt your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can reduce your riding skills. Any amount of alcohol makes it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass. A dashed line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists is:
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best foot protection when riding. Choose boots that are high and strong enough to cover and support your ankles.
